- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

1	---
2	redu_schema: 2
3	repo: https://github.com/metabase/metabase
4	plan:
5	  tool: deploy_compose
6	  image: metabase/metabase:v0.63.13
7	  port: 3000
8	  vm: m1.medium
9	  flavor_id: "3"
10	  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
11	  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0452
12	bootstrap:
13	  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
14	  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
15	  source: metabase
16	quirks:
17	  - "⛔ USE metabase/metabase WITH A v0 TAG. There are two images and they are two different licences: hub.docker.com/metabase/metabase is the AGPL open-source build, hub.docker.com/metabase/metabase-enterprise is under the Metabase Commercial License. Their versioning doc makes the leading digit the licence marker, so v0.x is open source and v1.x is enterprise. Handing a self-hoster the enterprise image is a licensing problem, not a preference."
18	  - "⚠️ DO NOT PICK THE TAG FROM GITHUB RELEASES. Measured 2026-08-16: the newest GitHub release is v0.63.2 (2026-07-29) while the newest stable image on Docker Hub is v0.63.13 (2026-08-14), and v0.63.3, v0.63.5, v0.63.10 and v0.63.13 have no GitHub release and no git tag at all. Check the Docker Hub tag list, pin an exact version (or the digest), and never use :latest or a floating v0.63.x, both of which move under you."
19	  - "⛔⛔ WITHOUT MB_DB_TYPE IT SILENTLY USES H2, INSIDE THE CONTAINER, AND THEIR DOCS SAY AVOID IT IN PRODUCTION IN THOSE WORDS. Worse than the usual version of this trap: Metabase FAILS OPEN. If the MB_DB_* values are wrong rather than missing, it does not error, it creates a brand new H2 database and boots happily, and the symptom is every dashboard disappearing after a restart. THE POST-DEPLOY CHECK IS ONE GREP: the startup log must NOT contain 'Verifying h2 Database Connection'. Run it every time; a healthy URL proves nothing here."
20	  - "DATABASE: set MB_DB_TYPE=postgres and remap redu's injected env onto MB_DB_HOST=\"${PGHOST}\", MB_DB_PORT=\"${PGPORT}\", MB_DB_DBNAME=\"${PGDATABASE}\", MB_DB_USER=\"${PGUSER}\", MB_DB_PASS=\"${PGPASSWORD}\". Note MB_DB_DBNAME and MB_DB_PASS, neither of which is spelled the way you would guess. MB_DB_CONNECTION_URI is a documented alternative that takes a full JDBC URI, and it is the better route if the password contains characters that need escaping. Metabase creates its own tables but will NOT create the database; redu's managed Postgres already provides one called `app`, so that is handled."
21	  - "⚠️ THE APP-DB SCHEMA MUST BE public. Their env var reference states outright that the currentSchema JDBC parameter has no effect and the schema for a Postgres application database must be public. redu's managed Postgres gives you public by default, so this is a non-issue here; it becomes one the moment someone points this at a database that hands out a per-tenant schema."
22	  - "⛔ SET MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY BEFORE ANYONE ADDS A DATA SOURCE. It is NOT required and defaults to null, which is exactly why it gets skipped. Without it, the credentials for every warehouse the user connects sit in cleartext in the managed Postgres, which is now a separate machine from the app and a separate blast radius. Generate it with `openssl rand -base64 32` (minimum 16 characters, base64). Two things make the timing matter: adding the key later does NOT retro-encrypt existing rows, you must reopen and save each database in the admin panel; and changing or losing it is not a restart problem, it is an offline CLI rotation with the OLD key (`rotate-encryption-key`), or else re-entering every connection by hand. Set it on day one and store it where it cannot be lost."
23	  - "⛔ SET MB_SITE_URL EXPLICITLY, AND UNDERSTAND WHY. Left unset, Metabase does not simply default: it takes the first non-healthcheck request, reads Origin, then X-Forwarded-Host, then Host, and PERSISTS that as the site URL in the application database. On a public hostname that means a spoofed Host header from the first visitor can set the value that later appears in password-reset and invitation emails. Separately, the scheme comes from X-Forwarded-Proto and friends, so a proxy that does not send one produces a persisted http:// URL on an https site, which breaks SSO redirects and auto-disables force-HTTPS. Environment variables take precedence and are never written into the app DB, so setting it is also the way to make it stable. Generate the dname yourself in the full `metabase-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form so the value is known at deploy time."
24	  - "⛔⛔ THE FIRST VISITOR CAN CLAIM THE INSTANCE. The account created by the first-run flow is an admin by default, /api/setup and /session are the two route groups mounted WITHOUT the auth wrapper, the setup token is a Setting with public visibility, and /api/session/properties returns public settings to anonymous callers. ⚠️ Labelled honestly: that chain is read from the source, NOT reproduced against a live instance, so treat it as a strong reason to close the window rather than as a demonstrated exploit. Either way the safe order is the same: complete the setup flow immediately, before you hand the URL to anyone, and confirm afterwards that /api/setup refuses with its 'can only be used to create the first user' error."
25	  - "NO PERSISTENT VOLUME IS NEEDED, AND THIS IS THE ONLY ENTRY IN THE LIBRARY WHERE THAT IS TRUE. The image declares no VOLUME in its 33-line Dockerfile, logs go to stdout, and with an external Postgres all state lives there. /plugins must be WRITABLE but not persistent: Metabase re-extracts its bundled drivers into it on every start. Only mount something there if the user adds third-party driver JARs. A disposable container is the correct shape here, so do not invent a volume out of habit."
26	  - "PORT 3000, MB_JETTY_PORT if it ever needs changing. Health endpoint is GET /api/health, which is also what their own compose example probes."
27	  - "SIZING AND THE OOM BEHAVIOUR. Upstream's baseline is 1 core and 1 GB, plus roughly 1 CPU and 2 GB for every 20 concurrent people, so m1.medium (2 vCPU / 4 GB) is a sensible default for a small team. Two things make undersizing sharp rather than gradual: the JVM takes about a quarter of machine RAM as its default heap, and their entrypoint bakes in -XX:+CrashOnOutOfMemoryError, so running out of heap KILLS THE CONTAINER instead of getting slow. Set JAVA_OPTS=-Xmx2g deliberately on m1.medium rather than accepting the default, and make sure the restart policy is in place."
28	  - "KEEP THE PROXY DUMB. Their troubleshooting docs name Cloudflare Rocket Loader, Cloudflare and Azure WAF, and Apache PageSpeed as causes of 'Save Failed', 403s and blank pages. redu terminates TLS and passes through, which is what Metabase wants. Do not add anything clever in front of it, and if the user later puts Cloudflare on a custom domain, remember this before debugging the app."
29	  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. Metabase creates and migrates its own tables at boot against the managed Postgres. First boot is slow: it is a JVM plus a schema build."
30	  - "NO SMTP ON A DEFAULT DEPLOY, so invitations and password resets do not send. Say so plainly; the admin account you create is the only way in until MB_EMAIL_* is wired to a provider the user owns."
31	  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.045/hr; fits the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '3' (m1.medium), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2' (m1.small; OMITTING db_flavor_id defaults the DB VM to the app flavor and doubles the bill), port 3000."
32	  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source, and the Metabase repo is very large. Write a one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."
33	  - "LICENCE: the metabase/metabase image is AGPL. The user runs their own instance in their own account, which is fine. Do not help anyone offer Metabase as a hosted service without meeting the AGPL's source-offer obligation, and do not substitute the enterprise image to get a feature."
34	  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY, the admin password and every warehouse connection belong to the user. Hand them over in the session; the deploy log records that the key was set, never its value."
35	  - "AFTERWARDS: pass THIS file to get_deployment as redu_md and write the merged redu_md_markdown back. Worth recording: the exact image tag you pinned, and whether the h2 log-grep came back clean."
36	  - "DELETING IT LOSES NOTHING IF THE DATABASE SURVIVES. Because there is no volume, delete_deployment removes a stateless container: every question, dashboard and collection is in the managed Postgres, which is deliberately kept and keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr. Redeploying against the same database brings the whole instance back. That is the opposite of Nextcloud in this library, and worth saying out loud."
37	---
38	
39	# Self-host Metabase on redu
40	
41	Dashboards and SQL questions over your own databases: one container, a managed Postgres beside it,
42	a public HTTPS URL. No volume, because the container is disposable and everything lives in the
43	database.
44	
45	## What this deploys
46	
47	- **Metabase**, the AGPL open-source build, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
48	- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM holding every question, dashboard and collection.
49	- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.
50	
51	About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time, and because there is no
52	volume, redeploying against the same database brings it all back.
53	
54	## Deploy
55	
56	Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
57	directory containing this file:
58	
59	    Read redu.md and deploy Metabase on redu.
60	
61	The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.
62	
63	## The three that actually break it
64	
65	**The application database fails open.** Metabase defaults to an embedded H2 database that its
66	own docs tell you to avoid in production, and if your Postgres settings are *wrong* rather than
67	missing it does not error: it quietly creates a fresh H2 and boots. The symptom is every dashboard
68	vanishing after a restart. The check is one grep of the startup log for
69	`Verifying h2 Database Connection`, which must not appear.
70	
71	**The encryption key.** `MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY` is optional, which is exactly why it gets
72	skipped. Without it, the credentials for every database you connect sit in cleartext in the
73	application database. Setting it later does not encrypt what is already there, and losing it means
74	re-entering every connection by hand.
75	
76	**The site URL.** Unset, Metabase takes the first request it sees, reads its headers, and
77	*persists* the result as the instance's public URL. That value ends up in password reset emails.
78	
79	## Two licences, one letter apart
80	
81	Metabase publishes two images. `metabase/metabase` is AGPL. `metabase/metabase-enterprise` is
82	under their commercial licence. Their version numbers encode it too: a leading `0` is open source,
83	a leading `1` is enterprise. This recipe pins the open-source one on purpose.
84	
85	## Deploy log
86	
87	- Not yet deployed. The first real run replaces this line with its measured time, flavor and
88	  hourly rate, and should record the exact image tag pinned and that the H2 log check came back
89	  clean.

Check the Docker Hub tag list, pin an exact version (or the digest), and never use :latest or a floating v0.63.x, both of which move under you."
  - "⛔⛔ WITHOUT MB_DB_TYPE IT SILENTLY USES H2, INSIDE THE CONTAINER, AND THEIR DOCS SAY AVOID IT IN PRODUCTION IN THOSE WORDS. Worse than the usual version of this trap: Metabase FAILS OPEN. If the MB_DB_* values are wrong rather than missing, it does not error, it creates a brand new H2 database and boots happily, and the symptom is every dashboard disappearing after a restart. THE POST-DEPLOY CHECK IS ONE GREP: the startup log must NOT contain 'Verifying h2 Database Connection'. Run it every time; a healthy URL proves nothing here."
  - "DATABASE: set MB_DB_TYPE=postgres and remap redu's injected env onto MB_DB_HOST=\"${PGHOST}\", MB_DB_PORT=\"${PGPORT}\", MB_DB_DBNAME=\"${PGDATABASE}\", MB_DB_USER=\"${PGUSER}\", MB_DB_PASS=\"${PGPASSWORD}\". Note MB_DB_DBNAME and MB_DB_PASS, neither of which is spelled the way you would guess. MB_DB_CONNECTION_URI is a documented alternative that takes a full JDBC URI, and it is the better route if the password contains characters that need escaping. Metabase creates its own tables but will NOT create the database; redu's managed Postgres already provides one called `app`, so that is handled."
  - "⚠️ THE APP-DB SCHEMA MUST BE public. Their env var reference states outright that the currentSchema JDBC parameter has no effect and the schema for a Postgres application database must be public. redu's managed Postgres gives you public by default, so this is a non-issue here; it becomes one the moment someone points this at a database that hands out a per-tenant schema."
  - "⛔ SET MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY BEFORE ANYONE ADDS A DATA SOURCE. It is NOT required and defaults to null, which is exactly why it gets skipped. Without it, the credentials for every warehouse the user connects sit in cleartext in the managed Postgres, which is now a separate machine from the app and a separate blast radius. Generate it with `openssl rand -base64 32` (minimum 16 characters, base64). Two things make the timing matter: adding the key later does NOT retro-encrypt existing rows, you must reopen and save each database in the admin panel; and changing or losing it is not a restart problem, it is an offline CLI rotation with the OLD key (`rotate-encryption-key`), or else re-entering every connection by hand. Set it on day one and store it where it cannot be lost."
  - "⛔ SET MB_SITE_URL EXPLICITLY, AND UNDERSTAND WHY. Left unset, Metabase does not simply default: it takes the first non-healthcheck request, reads Origin, then X-Forwarded-Host, then Host, and PERSISTS that as the site URL in the application database. On a public hostname that means a spoofed Host header from the first visitor can set the value that later appears in password-reset and invitation emails. Separately, the scheme comes from X-Forwarded-Proto and friends, so a proxy that does not send one produces a persisted http:// URL on an https site, which breaks SSO redirects and auto-disables force-HTTPS. Environment variables take precedence and are never written into the app DB, so setting it is also the way to make it stable. Generate the dname yourself in the full `metabase-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form so the value is known at deploy time."
  - "⛔⛔ THE FIRST VISITOR CAN CLAIM THE INSTANCE. The account created by the first-run flow is an admin by default, /api/setup and /session are the two route groups mounted WITHOUT the auth wrapper, the setup token is a Setting with public visibility, and /api/session/properties returns public settings to anonymous callers. ⚠️ Labelled honestly: that chain is read from the source, NOT reproduced against a live instance, so treat it as a strong reason to close the window rather than as a demonstrated exploit. Either way the safe order is the same: complete the setup flow immediately, before you hand the URL to anyone, and confirm afterwards that /api/setup refuses with its 'can only be used to create the first user' error."
  - "NO PERSISTENT VOLUME IS NEEDED, AND THIS IS THE ONLY ENTRY IN THE LIBRARY WHERE THAT IS TRUE. The image declares no VOLUME in its 33-line Dockerfile, logs go to stdout, and with an external Postgres all state lives there. /plugins must be WRITABLE but not persistent: Metabase re-extracts its bundled drivers into it on every start. Only mount something there if the user adds third-party driver JARs. A disposable container is the correct shape here, so do not invent a volume out of habit."
  - "PORT 3000, MB_JETTY_PORT if it ever needs changing. Health endpoint is GET /api/health, which is also what their own compose example probes."
  - "SIZING AND THE OOM BEHAVIOUR. Upstream's baseline is 1 core and 1 GB, plus roughly 1 CPU and 2 GB for every 20 concurrent people, so m1.medium (2 vCPU / 4 GB) is a sensible default for a small team. Two things make undersizing sharp rather than gradual: the JVM takes about a quarter of machine RAM as its default heap, and their entrypoint bakes in -XX:+CrashOnOutOfMemoryError, so running out of heap KILLS THE CONTAINER instead of getting slow. Set JAVA_OPTS=-Xmx2g deliberately on m1.medium rather than accepting the default, and make sure the restart policy is in place."
  - "KEEP THE PROXY DUMB. Their troubleshooting docs name Cloudflare Rocket Loader, Cloudflare and Azure WAF, and Apache PageSpeed as causes of 'Save Failed', 403s and blank pages. redu terminates TLS and passes through, which is what Metabase wants. Do not add anything clever in front of it, and if the user later puts Cloudflare on a custom domain, remember this before debugging the app."

  - "NO SMTP ON A DEFAULT DEPLOY, so invitations and password resets do not send. Say so plainly; the admin account you create is the only way in until MB_EMAIL_* is wired to a provider the user owns."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.045/hr; fits the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '3' (m1.medium), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2' (m1.small; OMITTING db_flavor_id defaults the DB VM to the app flavor and doubles the bill), port 3000."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source, and the Metabase repo is very large. Write a one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."

Redeploying against the same database brings the whole instance back. That is the opposite of Nextcloud in this library, and worth saying out loud."

# Self-host Metabase on redu

Dashboards and SQL questions over your own databases: one container, a managed Postgres beside it,
a public HTTPS URL. No volume, because the container is disposable and everything lives in the
database.

## What this deploys

- **Metabase**, the AGPL open-source build, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM holding every question, dashboard and collection.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time, and because there is no
volume, redeploying against the same database brings it all back.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Metabase on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**The application database fails open.** Metabase defaults to an embedded H2 database that its
own docs tell you to avoid in production, and if your Postgres settings are *wrong* rather than
missing it does not error: it quietly creates a fresh H2 and boots. The symptom is every dashboard
vanishing after a restart. The check is one grep of the startup log for
`Verifying h2 Database Connection`, which must not appear.

**The encryption key.** `MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY` is optional, which is exactly why it gets
skipped. Without it, the credentials for every database you connect sit in cleartext in the
application database. Setting it later does not encrypt what is already there, and losing it means
re-entering every connection by hand.

**The site URL.** Unset, Metabase takes the first request it sees, reads its headers, and
*persists* the result as the instance's public URL. That value ends up in password reset emails.

## Two licences, one letter apart

Metabase publishes two images. `metabase/metabase` is AGPL. `metabase/metabase-enterprise` is
under their commercial licence. Their version numbers encode it too: a leading `0` is open source,
a leading `1` is enterprise. This recipe pins the open-source one on purpose.

## Deploy log

- Not yet deployed. The first real run replaces this line with its measured time, flavor and
  hourly rate, and should record the exact image tag pinned and that the H2 log check came back
  clean.

MB_DB_CONNECTION_URI is a documented alternative that takes a full JDBC URI, and it is the better route if the password contains characters that need escaping. On a public hostname that means a spoofed Host header from the first visitor can set the value that later appears in password-reset and invitation emails. Separately, the scheme comes from X-Forwarded-Proto and friends, so a proxy that does not send one produces a persisted http:// URL on an https site, which breaks SSO redirects and auto-disables force-HTTPS. # Self-host Metabase on redu

Dashboards and SQL questions over your own databases: one container, a managed Postgres beside it,
a public HTTPS URL. No volume, because the container is disposable and everything lives in the
database.

## What this deploys

- **Metabase**, the AGPL open-source build, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM holding every question, dashboard and collection.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time, and because there is no
volume, redeploying against the same database brings it all back.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Metabase on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**The application database fails open.** Metabase defaults to an embedded H2 database that its
own docs tell you to avoid in production, and if your Postgres settings are *wrong* rather than
missing it does not error: it quietly creates a fresh H2 and boots. The symptom is every dashboard
vanishing after a restart. The check is one grep of the startup log for
`Verifying h2 Database Connection`, which must not appear.

**The encryption key.** `MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY` is optional, which is exactly why it gets
skipped. Without it, the credentials for every database you connect sit in cleartext in the
application database. Setting it later does not encrypt what is already there, and losing it means
re-entering every connection by hand.

**The site URL.** Unset, Metabase takes the first request it sees, reads its headers, and
*persists* the result as the instance's public URL. That value ends up in password reset emails.

## Two licences, one letter apart

Metabase publishes two images. `metabase/metabase` is AGPL. `metabase/metabase-enterprise` is
under their commercial licence. Their version numbers encode it too: a leading `0` is open source,
a leading `1` is enterprise. This recipe pins the open-source one on purpose.

## Deploy log

- Not yet deployed. The first real run replaces this line with its measured time, flavor and
  hourly rate, and should record the exact image tag pinned and that the H2 log check came back
  clean.

m1.small - 1 vCPU / 2048 MB")] end app -->|"5432 (private)"| pg ``` No persistent volume. Re-checked on Docker Hub today: still the newest stable v0.63.x. | | `MB_DB_TYPE` | `postgres` | Without it Metabase silently creates an in-container H2 DB and boots happily. | | `MB_DB_*` | remapped from redu's `PG*` env | `MB_DB_DBNAME` / `MB_DB_PASS` are not spelled the obvious way. | | `MB_SITE_URL` | `https://metabase-5w3f7can.redu.cloud` | Unset, Metabase persists whatever the first request's headers say. dname generated up front so the value is known at deploy time. | | `MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY` | generated (`openssl rand -base64 32`) | Set before the first data source, or warehouse credentials sit in cleartext in Postgres. Setting it later does not retro-encrypt. | | `JAVA_OPTS` | `-Xmx2g` | The entrypoint bakes in `-XX:+CrashOnOutOfMemoryError` — out-of-heap kills the container. | | `restart` | `unless-stopped` | Must come back on every boot. | | `migrate_command` | none | Metabase creates and migrates its own tables at boot. First boot is slow (JVM + schema build). | ## Post-deploy checks 1. **The H2 grep** — the startup log must NOT contain `Verifying h2 Database Connection`. A healthy URL proves nothing here; Metabase fails open to H2. 2. **Claim the instance immediately** — the first-run flow creates an admin, and `/api/setup` is mounted without the auth wrapper. Complete setup before the URL is shared, then confirm `/api/setup` refuses with its "can only be used to create the first user" error. ## Known gaps on a default deploy - **No SMTP.** Invitations and password resets will not send until `MB_EMAIL_*` is wired to a provider you own. The admin account created at setup is the only way in. - **Keep the proxy dumb.** redu terminates TLS and passes through, which is what Metabase wants. Cloudflare Rocket Loader / WAF are documented causes of "Save Failed" and blank pages. _Generated by redu plan_deploy, adjusted to the sizing recorded in redu.md. Confirm before provisioning._

# Self-host Metabase on redu

Dashboards and SQL questions over your own databases: one container, a managed Postgres beside it,
a public HTTPS URL. No volume, because the container is disposable and everything lives in the
database.

## What this deploys

- **Metabase**, the AGPL open-source build, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM holding every question, dashboard and collection.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time, and because there is no
volume, redeploying against the same database brings it all back.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Metabase on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**The application database fails open.** Metabase defaults to an embedded H2 database that its
own docs tell you to avoid in production, and if your Postgres settings are *wrong* rather than
missing it does not error: it quietly creates a fresh H2 and boots. The symptom is every dashboard
vanishing after a restart. The check is one grep of the startup log for
`Verifying h2 Database Connection`, which must not appear — run it with `sudo docker logs metabase`,
because the VM has no podman and a typo'd engine name turns the check into a guaranteed pass.

**The encryption key.** `MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY` is optional, which is exactly why it gets
skipped. Without it, the credentials for every database you connect sit in cleartext in the
application database. Setting it later does not encrypt what is already there, and losing it means
re-entering every connection by hand.

**The site URL.** Unset, Metabase takes the first request it sees, reads its headers, and
*persists* the result as the instance's public URL. That value ends up in password reset emails.

## Two licences, one letter apart

Metabase publishes two images. `metabase/metabase` is AGPL. `metabase/metabase-enterprise` is
under their commercial licence. Their version numbers encode it too: a leading `0` is open source,
a leading `1` is enterprise. This recipe pins the open-source one on purpose.

## Deploy log

- 2026-08-16 deploy #426: ready in ~4 min on m1.medium (flavor_id "3") + managed Postgres m1.small
  (db #129), GBP 0.0452/hr. Image pinned `metabase/metabase:v0.63.13`, re-verified that day as the
  newest stable v0.63.x on Docker Hub. H2 log-grep came back CLEAN (0 matches) and positively
  confirmed `Successfully verified PostgreSQL 16.14 application database connection`.
  MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY set before first boot. No volume, no migrate_command.

---
last_deploy:
  id: 426
  date: 2026-08-16
  status: ready
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/metabase/metabase
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: metabase/metabase:v0.63.13
  port: 3000
  vm: m1.medium
  flavor_id: "3"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0452
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: metabase
quirks:
  - "⛔ USE metabase/metabase WITH A v0 TAG. There are two images and they are two different licences: hub.docker.com/metabase/metabase is the AGPL open-source build, hub.docker.com/metabase/metabase-enterprise is under the Metabase Commercial License. Their versioning doc makes the leading digit the licence marker, so v0.x is open source and v1.x is enterprise. Handing a self-hoster the enterprise image is a licensing problem, not a preference."
  - "⚠️ DO NOT PICK THE TAG FROM GITHUB RELEASES. Measured 2026-08-16: the newest GitHub release is v0.63.2 (2026-07-29) while the newest stable image on Docker Hub is v0.63.13 (2026-08-14), and v0.63.3, v0.63.5, v0.63.10 and v0.63.13 have no GitHub release and no git tag at all. Check the Docker Hub tag list, pin an exact version (or the digest), and never use :latest or a floating v0.63.x, both of which move under you."
  - "⛔⛔ WITHOUT MB_DB_TYPE IT SILENTLY USES H2, INSIDE THE CONTAINER, AND THEIR DOCS SAY AVOID IT IN PRODUCTION IN THOSE WORDS. Worse than the usual version of this trap: Metabase FAILS OPEN. If the MB_DB_* values are wrong rather than missing, it does not error, it creates a brand new H2 database and boots happily, and the symptom is every dashboard disappearing after a restart. THE POST-DEPLOY CHECK IS ONE GREP: the startup log must NOT contain 'Verifying h2 Database Connection'. Run it every time; a healthy URL proves nothing here."
  - "DATABASE: set MB_DB_TYPE=postgres and remap redu's injected env onto MB_DB_HOST=\"${PGHOST}\", MB_DB_PORT=\"${PGPORT}\", MB_DB_DBNAME=\"${PGDATABASE}\", MB_DB_USER=\"${PGUSER}\", MB_DB_PASS=\"${PGPASSWORD}\". Note MB_DB_DBNAME and MB_DB_PASS, neither of which is spelled the way you would guess. MB_DB_CONNECTION_URI is a documented alternative that takes a full JDBC URI, and it is the better route if the password contains characters that need escaping. Metabase creates its own tables but will NOT create the database; redu's managed Postgres already provides one called `app`, so that is handled."
  - "⚠️ THE APP-DB SCHEMA MUST BE public. Their env var reference states outright that the currentSchema JDBC parameter has no effect and the schema for a Postgres application database must be public. redu's managed Postgres gives you public by default, so this is a non-issue here; it becomes one the moment someone points this at a database that hands out a per-tenant schema."
  - "⛔ SET MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY BEFORE ANYONE ADDS A DATA SOURCE. It is NOT required and defaults to null, which is exactly why it gets skipped. Without it, the credentials for every warehouse the user connects sit in cleartext in the managed Postgres, which is now a separate machine from the app and a separate blast radius. Generate it with `openssl rand -base64 32` (minimum 16 characters, base64). Two things make the timing matter: adding the key later does NOT retro-encrypt existing rows, you must reopen and save each database in the admin panel; and changing or losing it is not a restart problem, it is an offline CLI rotation with the OLD key (`rotate-encryption-key`), or else re-entering every connection by hand. Set it on day one and store it where it cannot be lost."
  - "⛔ SET MB_SITE_URL EXPLICITLY, AND UNDERSTAND WHY. Left unset, Metabase does not simply default: it takes the first non-healthcheck request, reads Origin, then X-Forwarded-Host, then Host, and PERSISTS that as the site URL in the application database. On a public hostname that means a spoofed Host header from the first visitor can set the value that later appears in password-reset and invitation emails. Separately, the scheme comes from X-Forwarded-Proto and friends, so a proxy that does not send one produces a persisted http:// URL on an https site, which breaks SSO redirects and auto-disables force-HTTPS. Environment variables take precedence and are never written into the app DB, so setting it is also the way to make it stable. Generate the dname yourself in the full `metabase-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form so the value is known at deploy time."
  - "⛔⛔ THE FIRST VISITOR CAN CLAIM THE INSTANCE. The account created by the first-run flow is an admin by default, /api/setup and /session are the two route groups mounted WITHOUT the auth wrapper, the setup token is a Setting with public visibility, and /api/session/properties returns public settings to anonymous callers. ⚠️ Labelled honestly: that chain is read from the source, NOT reproduced against a live instance, so treat it as a strong reason to close the window rather than as a demonstrated exploit. Either way the safe order is the same: complete the setup flow immediately, before you hand the URL to anyone, and confirm afterwards that /api/setup refuses with its 'can only be used to create the first user' error."
  - "NO PERSISTENT VOLUME IS NEEDED, AND THIS IS THE ONLY ENTRY IN THE LIBRARY WHERE THAT IS TRUE. The image declares no VOLUME in its 33-line Dockerfile, logs go to stdout, and with an external Postgres all state lives there. /plugins must be WRITABLE but not persistent: Metabase re-extracts its bundled drivers into it on every start. Only mount something there if the user adds third-party driver JARs. A disposable container is the correct shape here, so do not invent a volume out of habit."
  - "PORT 3000, MB_JETTY_PORT if it ever needs changing. Health endpoint is GET /api/health, which is also what their own compose example probes."
  - "SIZING AND THE OOM BEHAVIOUR. Upstream's baseline is 1 core and 1 GB, plus roughly 1 CPU and 2 GB for every 20 concurrent people, so m1.medium (2 vCPU / 4 GB) is a sensible default for a small team. Two things make undersizing sharp rather than gradual: the JVM takes about a quarter of machine RAM as its default heap, and their entrypoint bakes in -XX:+CrashOnOutOfMemoryError, so running out of heap KILLS THE CONTAINER instead of getting slow. Set JAVA_OPTS=-Xmx2g deliberately on m1.medium rather than accepting the default, and make sure the restart policy is in place."
  - "KEEP THE PROXY DUMB. Their troubleshooting docs name Cloudflare Rocket Loader, Cloudflare and Azure WAF, and Apache PageSpeed as causes of 'Save Failed', 403s and blank pages. redu terminates TLS and passes through, which is what Metabase wants. Do not add anything clever in front of it, and if the user later puts Cloudflare on a custom domain, remember this before debugging the app."
  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. Metabase creates and migrates its own tables at boot against the managed Postgres. First boot is slow: it is a JVM plus a schema build."
  - "NO SMTP ON A DEFAULT DEPLOY, so invitations and password resets do not send. Say so plainly; the admin account you create is the only way in until MB_EMAIL_* is wired to a provider the user owns."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.045/hr; fits the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '3' (m1.medium), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2' (m1.small; OMITTING db_flavor_id defaults the DB VM to the app flavor and doubles the bill), port 3000."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source, and the Metabase repo is very large. Write a one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."
  - "LICENCE: the metabase/metabase image is AGPL. The user runs their own instance in their own account, which is fine. Do not help anyone offer Metabase as a hosted service without meeting the AGPL's source-offer obligation, and do not substitute the enterprise image to get a feature."
  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY, the admin password and every warehouse connection belong to the user. Hand them over in the session; the deploy log records that the key was set, never its value."
  - "AFTERWARDS: pass THIS file to get_deployment as redu_md and write the merged redu_md_markdown back. Worth recording: the exact image tag you pinned, and whether the h2 log-grep came back clean."
  - "DELETING IT LOSES NOTHING IF THE DATABASE SURVIVES. Because there is no volume, delete_deployment removes a stateless container: every question, dashboard and collection is in the managed Postgres, which is deliberately kept and keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr. Redeploying against the same database brings the whole instance back. That is the opposite of Nextcloud in this library, and worth saying out loud."
  - "⚠️ THE VM RUNS DOCKER, NOT PODMAN, so the h2 log-grep must be `sudo docker logs metabase`. Measured 2026-08-16 on deploy #426: `sudo podman logs metabase` returns 'command not found', and piping that into `grep -c 'Verifying h2 Database Connection'` prints 0 — a clean-looking pass produced entirely by the error message. The check that is supposed to catch a silent H2 fallback silently passes instead. Always confirm POSITIVELY as well: the log must contain 'Verifying postgres Database Connection' and 'Successfully verified PostgreSQL <version> application database connection'."
  - "plan_deploy SIZES THIS AT m1.large, NOT the m1.medium recorded here, because needs_compose:true raises the app VM to a build-capable floor. It surfaces the disagreement as a `flavor-differs-from-record` preflight rather than resolving it. Nothing is built here (the image is pulled), so m1.medium is right and you must pass flavor_id '3' EXPLICITLY; accepting the plan's default silently moves the bill from GBP 0.0452/hr to GBP 0.066/hr."
  - "TIMING, measured 2026-08-16 on deploy #426: provisioning to ready took about 4 minutes end to end, most of it the ~600 MB image pull, and /api/health answered 200 roughly 3 minutes after the compose phase began. The Liquibase schema build against an empty Postgres is a small part of it. Do not treat the first two minutes of 000/502 as a failure."
---

# Self-host Metabase on redu

Dashboards and SQL questions over your own databases: one container, a managed Postgres beside it,
a public HTTPS URL. No volume, because the container is disposable and everything lives in the
database.

## What this deploys

- **Metabase**, the AGPL open-source build, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM holding every question, dashboard and collection.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time, and because there is no
volume, redeploying against the same database brings it all back.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Metabase on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**The application database fails open.** Metabase defaults to an embedded H2 database that its
own docs tell you to avoid in production, and if your Postgres settings are *wrong* rather than
missing it does not error: it quietly creates a fresh H2 and boots. The symptom is every dashboard
vanishing after a restart. The check is one grep of the startup log for
`Verifying h2 Database Connection`, which must not appear — run it with `sudo docker logs metabase`,
because the VM has no podman and a typo'd engine name turns the check into a guaranteed pass.

**The encryption key.** `MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY` is optional, which is exactly why it gets
skipped. Without it, the credentials for every database you connect sit in cleartext in the
application database. Setting it later does not encrypt what is already there, and losing it means
re-entering every connection by hand.

**The site URL.** Unset, Metabase takes the first request it sees, reads its headers, and
*persists* the result as the instance's public URL. That value ends up in password reset emails.

## Two licences, one letter apart

Metabase publishes two images. `metabase/metabase` is AGPL. `metabase/metabase-enterprise` is
under their commercial licence. Their version numbers encode it too: a leading `0` is open source,
a leading `1` is enterprise. This recipe pins the open-source one on purpose.

## Deploy log

- 2026-08-16 deploy #426: ready in ~4 min on m1.medium (flavor_id "3") + managed Postgres m1.small
  (db #129), GBP 0.0452/hr. Image pinned `metabase/metabase:v0.63.13`, re-verified that day as the
  newest stable v0.63.x on Docker Hub. H2 log-grep came back CLEAN (0 matches) and positively
  confirmed `Successfully verified PostgreSQL 16.14 application database connection`.
  MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY set before first boot. No volume, no migrate_command.
- 2026-08-16 deploy #426: ready, https://metabase-5w3f7can.redu.cloud.

45	
46	# Self-host Metabase on redu
47	
48	Dashboards and SQL questions over your own databases: one container, a managed Postgres beside it,
49	a public HTTPS URL. No volume, because the container is disposable and everything lives in the
50	database.
51	
52	## What this deploys
53	
54	- **Metabase**, the AGPL open-source build, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
55	- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM holding every question, dashboard and collection.
56	- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.
57	
58	About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time, and because there is no
59	volume, redeploying against the same database brings it all back.
60	
61	## Deploy
62	
63	Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
64	directory containing this file:
65	
66	    Read redu.md and deploy Metabase on redu.
67	
68	The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.
69	
70	## The three that actually break it
71	
72	**The application database fails open.** Metabase defaults to an embedded H2 database that its
73	own docs tell you to avoid in production, and if your Postgres settings are *wrong* rather than
74	missing it does not error: it quietly creates a fresh H2 and boots. The symptom is every dashboard
75	vanishing after a restart. The check is one grep of the startup log for
76	`Verifying h2 Database Connection`, which must not appear — run it with `sudo docker logs metabase`,
77	because the VM has no podman and a typo'd engine name turns the check into a guaranteed pass.
78	
79	**The encryption key.** `MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY` is optional, which is exactly why it gets
80	skipped. Without it, the credentials for every database you connect sit in cleartext in the
81	application database. Setting it later does not encrypt what is already there, and losing it means
82	re-entering every connection by hand.
83	
84	**The site URL.** Unset, Metabase takes the first request it sees, reads its headers, and
85	*persists* the result as the instance's public URL. That value ends up in password reset emails.
86	
87	## Two licences, one letter apart
88	
89	Metabase publishes two images. `metabase/metabase` is AGPL. `metabase/metabase-enterprise` is
90	under their commercial licence. Their version numbers encode it too: a leading `0` is open source,
91	a leading `1` is enterprise. This recipe pins the open-source one on purpose.
92	
93	## Deploy log
94	
95	- 2026-08-16 deploy #426: ready in ~4 min on m1.medium (flavor_id "3") + managed Postgres m1.small
96	  (db #129), GBP 0.0452/hr. Image pinned `metabase/metabase:v0.63.13`, re-verified that day as the
97	  newest stable v0.63.x on Docker Hub. H2 log-grep came back CLEAN (0 matches) and positively
98	  confirmed `Successfully verified PostgreSQL 16.14 application database connection`.
99	  MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY set before first boot. No volume, no migrate_command.
100	- 2026-08-16 deploy #426: ready, https://metabase-5w3f7can.redu.cloud.
101	
102

# Self-host Metabase on redu

Dashboards and SQL questions over your own databases: one container, a managed Postgres beside it,
a public HTTPS URL. No volume, because the container is disposable and everything lives in the
database.

## What this deploys

- **Metabase**, the AGPL open-source build, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM holding every question, dashboard and collection.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time, and because there is no
volume, redeploying against the same database brings it all back.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Metabase on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**The application database fails open.** Metabase defaults to an embedded H2 database that its
own docs tell you to avoid in production, and if your Postgres settings are *wrong* rather than
missing it does not error: it quietly creates a fresh H2 and boots. The symptom is every dashboard
vanishing after a restart. The check is one grep of the startup log for
`Verifying h2 Database Connection`, which must not appear — run it with `sudo docker logs metabase`,
because the VM has no podman and a typo'd engine name turns the check into a guaranteed pass.

**The encryption key.** `MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY` is optional, which is exactly why it gets
skipped. Without it, the credentials for every database you connect sit in cleartext in the
application database. Setting it later does not encrypt what is already there, and losing it means
re-entering every connection by hand.

**The site URL.** Unset, Metabase takes the first request it sees, reads its headers, and
*persists* the result as the instance's public URL. That value ends up in password reset emails.

## Two licences, one letter apart

Metabase publishes two images. `metabase/metabase` is AGPL. `metabase/metabase-enterprise` is
under their commercial licence. Their version numbers encode it too: a leading `0` is open source,
a leading `1` is enterprise. This recipe pins the open-source one on purpose.

# Session report — Metabase on redu (deploy #426)

**Date:** 2026-08-16 / 2026-08-17
**Operator account:** «REDACTED:env:013044ef»
**Working directory:** `/home/milos/Desktop/tests_lib/metabase`
**Outcome:** deployed, verified, claimed, documented, then destroyed at the user's request. **Billing for this stack is now zero.**

---

## 1. What was asked

Three instructions across the session:

1. "Read redu.md and deploy Metabase on redu."
2. "create me an account there please"
3. "Write a full report on everything you did in this session (.md). Destroy this deployment."

All three were completed.

---

## 2. Timeline of actions

| # | Action | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Read `redu.md` (recipe with 20 recorded quirks) | Plan understood: `deploy_compose`, upload mode, m1.medium, managed Postgres |
| 2 | `whoami` + `check_deploy_prerequisites` | Account verified; network + keypair `redu-deploy-test` auto-selected |
| 3 | Re-checked the image tag on Docker Hub | `v0.63.13` still the newest stable `v0.63.x` — recipe's pin still correct |
| 4 | Generated dname + encryption key locally | `metabase-5w3f7can.redu.cloud`, key via `openssl rand -base64 32` |
| 5 | Wrote `docker-compose.yml` | One service, no volume, explicit env |
| 6 | `plan_deploy` (pasting `redu.md` + compose) | Plan + preflight returned; **flagged a sizing disagreement** (see §5) |
| 7 | Wrote `redu-deploy-plan.md`, showed plan + cost, **waited for approval** | User approved at m1.medium |
| 8 | `prepare_upload` → tar + curl | 7402 bytes, size verified against the upload response |
| 9 | `deploy_compose` | Deployment #426 created |
| 10 | Polled to `ready` | Ready in ~4 min |
| 11 | **Post-deploy verification** | All checks passed (see §4) |
| 12 | Merged the deploy record back into `redu.md` | Server-side merge, +3 quirks |
| 13 | Created the admin account via `/api/setup` | Instance claimed, window closed |
| 14 | Verified the claim + audited settings | Found the tracking bug (see §6), +3 more quirks |
| 15 | `delete_deployment` + `delete_database` | Both confirmed gone (see §8) |

---

## 3. What was deployed

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Image | `metabase/metabase:v0.63.13` (AGPL open-source build) |
| Deployment id | #426 |
| URL | `https://metabase-5w3f7can.redu.cloud` (dname generated up front, not auto-assigned) |
| App VM | m1.medium — 2 vCPU / 4096 MB — `b69cd474-dde8-4e2f-bdd7-ed5316267480`, private IP [ip] |
| Managed Postgres | db #129, VM `db-metabase`, m1.small, private IP [ip], PostgreSQL 16.14 |
| Port | 3000 |
| Volume | none — by design |
| Cost | GBP 0.0452/hr (~GBP 32.99/mo) |
| Provision → ready | ~4 minutes, mostly the ~600 MB image pull |

Environment set on the container:

```
MB_DB_TYPE=postgres          MB_SITE_URL=https://metabase-5w3f7can.redu.cloud
MB_DB_HOST=${PGHOST}         MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY=[REDACTED:value], handed over in session>
MB_DB_PORT=${PGPORT}         MB_JETTY_PORT=3000
MB_DB_DBNAME=${PGDATABASE}   JAVA_OPTS=-Xmx2g
MB_DB_USER=${PGUSER}         restart: unless-stopped
MB_DB_PASS=[REDACTED:value]}
```

---

## 4. Verification performed

Nothing below was assumed; each row was executed against the live instance.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/health` | `{"status":"ok"}` |
| **H2 grep** — `Verifying h2 Database Connection` in startup log | **0 matches** |
| Positive app-DB confirmation | `Verifying postgres Database Connection ...` → `Successfully verified PostgreSQL 16.14 (Ubuntu 16.14-0ubuntu0.24.04.1) application database connection` |
| `MB_SITE_URL` inside the container | `https://metabase-5w3f7can.redu.cloud` |

---

## 5. Judgement calls made

**Sizing — deployed at m1.medium, not the auto-planned m1.large.**
`plan_deploy` raised the app VM to m1.large (GBP 0.066/hr) because `needs_compose: true` triggers a
build-capable floor, and it surfaced the conflict with `redu.md` as a `flavor-differs-from-record`
preflight rather than resolving it. Nothing is built here — the image is pulled — so the floor did
not apply. Passed `flavor_id "3"` explicitly and presented both options to the user, who chose
m1.medium. **Saved GBP 0.021/hr (~GBP 15/mo) versus accepting the default.**

**Admin email — asked rather than guessed.**
Two plausible addresses were in play (`«REDACTED:env:013044ef»` from the redu account,
`«REDACTED:env:c5eef326»` from the Claude Code account). With no SMTP there is no password-reset path, so
